NATO.wiki: The military alliance of 32 European and North American democracies dedicated to mutual defense under Article 5 of the Washington Treaty.

VJTF.definition: Very High Readiness Joint Task Force
VJTF.wiki: NATO's highest-readiness spearhead force, capable of deploying an initial brigade-sized joint element to any flank within 48 to 72 hours of activation.

eFP.wiki: NATO's forward multinational battlegroups stationed permanently on a rotational basis in the Baltic states, Poland, Romania, and Bulgaria to deter adversary aggression.

C2.wiki: The facilities, communications, procedures, and personnel used by commanders to plan, direct, coordinate, and control military forces in tactical combat.

EW.wiki: Military actions exploiting the electromagnetic spectrum, including GPS jamming, communications intercept, drone spoofing, and radar counter-measures.

UAV.wiki: Remotely piloted or autonomous aircraft used extensively for real-time artillery spotting, frontline reconnaissance, and precision strike with loitering munitions.

SAM.wiki: Air defense systems (ranging from MANPADS to medium- and long-range batteries like Patriot and S-300/400) deployed to contest airspace and shoot down attack jets, cruise missiles, and drones.

IFV.wiki: Armored combat vehicles designed to carry infantry squads into direct combat while providing heavy direct autocannon and anti-tank guided missile fire support.

MBT.wiki: Heavily armored, tracked combat vehicles mounting a high-velocity main gun, providing mobile direct-fire punch and shock action for mechanized breakthrough operations.

CAS.wiki: Air attacks against hostile targets in close proximity to friendly ground troops, requiring detailed coordination and target deconfliction with forward controllers.

ISR.wiki: Integrated intelligence gathering using aerial drones, optical reconnaissance satellites, radar systems, and radio intercept to track enemy concentrations.

HIMARS.definition: M142 High Mobility Artillery Rocket System
HIMARS.wiki: A light multiple rocket launcher mounted on a standard medium tactical vehicle frame, firing GPS-guided GMLRS rockets for deep precision strikes behind enemy lines.

ATGM.wiki: Man-portable or vehicle-mounted guided missiles (such as Javelin, NLAW, and Spike) designed to penetrate and destroy heavy armor at long ranges.
